managementPlan.title: Management Plan
managementPlan.subtitle: over the year

inputs.1: Identification of ergonomic concerns arising from interviews or spontaneous employee search, from EHS records and from the health team.
inputs.2: Visits at work stations to monitor work activities and basic (qualitative) ergonomic analysis to identify ergonomic risk and route solutions.
inputs.3: Workstation visits to monitor work activities and advanced ergonomic analysis (quantitative) for ergonomic risk classification, prioritization of actions and solution planning.
inputs.4: Monitoring of the effectiveness of the improvements implemented with reassessment and reclassification of the risks and validation of the employees involved in the tasks.

outputs.1: Ergonomic awareness of the employees on the site, involvement of the ergonomics team with the other areas and identification of concerns on the site.
outputs.2: Basic analysis of the work activities and concerns in the site and participation of the Lean, Projects and Maintenance team to implement simple and administrative improvements. Accompaniment of the ergonomics team during the implementations.
outputs.3: Advanced analysis of work activities with the participation of Lean, Projects and Maintenance team to implement improvements and projects involving investments. Accompaniment of the ergonomics team during the implementations.
outputs.4: Compliance with pre-determined deadlines according to prioritization of actions with recorded changes and information of activity analyzed, ergonomic risk, action priority, investment involved and effectiveness of the action.

educational.1: Basic ergonomic training for all to identify ergonomic hazards and postural orientations at work.
educational.2: Advanced Ergonomics Training for Ergonomics Committee and Health teams, Moc / Changes, Projects, Lean, Incident / accident investigation.
educational.3: Advanced ergonomics training for procedures staff (SOPs or RAs)
educational.4: Program of training with recycling and guarantee of the update in the site with the theme ergonomics, including of new employees.

clinical.1: Ergo leader's involvement in health campaigns with themes related to Dorts prevention.
clinical.2: Investigation of medical / clinical occurrences with participation of Ergonomics Team member and EHS.
clinical.3: Health team involved in the selection of people (admission and periodical).
clinical.4: Postural, admission and periodic evaluation and monitoring program.

projects.1: Ergo leader participating in the MOC Team / Changes / Projects / Lean.
projects.2: Computerized data recording with Management Plan, Program Guidelines, Assessments, Risks and Projects.
projects.3: Involvement of the Ergonomics team with Managers, Ehs, Rh, Health, Manufacturing and Employees to prioritize actions and ergonomic improvement projects.
projects.4: Moc/Changes Systems and Computerized Procedures and registration of projects implemented in the site.

management.1: Ergo leader and Ergonomics Committee training.
management.2: Computerized data recording with Management Plan, Program Guidelines, Assessments, Risks and Projects.
management.3: Prioritization of ergonomics actions and monitoring projects and meeting deadlines.
management.4: Evaluation of the goals of Management and the Program of Ergonomics with Map of Risks and Projects of the site.

checklist.legendTitle: In each of the items surveyed, and also for the total items of this Check-list, consider

questions.question1: Is the distance between the back of a terminal and the nearest operator more than 1 m?
questions.question2: When it is necessary to use a diskette, CD or USB drive, are the respective devices easy to access?
questions.question3: Is there any equipment or material that impairs body positioning?
questions.question4: Is the temperature comfortable for the worker?
questions.question5: Is the workstation positioned sideways to the windows? Otherwise, do the windows have blinds and curtains?
questions.question6: Does the floor glare bother the eyes?
questions.question7: Are there burned-out bulbs near the workstation?
questions.question8: Are there any noises that bother the worker or impair their concentration?
questions.question9: Is the worker in the correct position for the type of job? (sitting or standing)
questions.question10: Is it possible to alternate posture so as to stand occasionally? (sitting or standing occasionally)
questions.question11: Has the worker received postural guidance?
questions.question12: Is there any factor that makes it necessary to work with a static contraction of the trunk?
questions.question13: Does the worker currently report any discomfort?
questions.question14: Are there breaks/rest of 10 minutes every 2 hours worked?
questions.question15: If the work involves only computer use, is there a 10-minute break every 50 minutes worked? (Typing)
questions.question16: When typing, is the average number of keystrokes less than 8,000 per hour?
questions.question17: Does the backrest support the dorsal-lumbar region?
questions.question18: Do the backrest and the seat allow a 100° angle?
questions.question19: Does the height of the chair seat allow a 90° angle of the knees?
questions.question20: Does the height of the armrests allow a 90° angle of the elbows?
questions.question21: Does it have padded, soft and adjustable armrests?
questions.question22: Is the upholstery made of a fabric that allows perspiration?
questions.question24: Is the monitor located in front of the worker?
questions.question25: Is there a height adjustment of the monitor?
questions.question26: Is there a tilt adjustment of the monitor?
questions.question27: Does the height of the monitor screen allow the worker's horizontal gaze?
questions.question28: Is the distance from the monitor screen to the worker's eyes between 50 and 70 cm?
questions.question29: Is the reading angle from the monitor screen to the eyes between 33° and 44°?
questions.question30: Is there brightness and character contrast control?
questions.question31: When working with spreadsheets, is the zoom below 100%?
questions.question33: Are there natural light reflections (from the windows) on the monitor screen?
questions.question34: Are there artificial light reflections (from the lamps) on the monitor screen?
questions.question35: Does the desk have height adjustment?
questions.question36: Does the desk height allow enough leg room?
questions.question37: Does the desk height allow proper adjustment of the arm/elbow support on the chair?
questions.question39: Is the desk surface made of non-reflective material?
questions.question41: Are the frequently used objects on the desk (keyboard, mouse, phone, calculator, documents) within the normal reach area (semicircles made with the elbows bent)?
questions.question42: Are the occasionally used objects on the desk within the maximum reach area (semicircles made with the elbows extended)?
questions.question44: Is it properly configured? (accents, language, etc.)
questions.question45: Does it take up too much space at the workstation?
questions.question47: Does it radiate heat to the worker's body?
questions.question48: Is there a keyboard wrist rest?
questions.question49: Is there a mouse wrist rest?
questions.question50: Is there a headset? If it is not needed, score yes
questions.question51: Is there a footrest? If it is not needed, score yes
questions.question52: If documents are frequently read for typing, is there a document holder? If it is not needed, score yes
questions.question53: Is there a stand to raise the screen of the equipment? Or is there a monitor?

questions.question1: Does the new design / modification generate manual handling of parts and / or equipment weighing more than 20 kg? If so, how? Are ergonomic devices and accessories available for items weighing > 20.0 kg or for parts whose handling is hampered by large dimensions or few handles?
questions.question2: Are ergonomic devices available to perform tasks that require effort to push or pull parts / equipment, regardless of distance? Which ones?
questions.question3: Does the work area / workplace offer functional space allowing alternation of posture? (the functional area should avoid prolonged forced postures of the trunk and / or body segments)
questions.question4: For work in the standing position, is the height of the bench(es) / table(s) compatible with the characteristics below, and are there seats for alternating posture? Heavy work: 73 to 95 cm; Light work: 86.5 to 107 cm; Precision work: 98 to 119 cm.
questions.question5: Does this design / modification pose an ergonomic repetitiveness risk for any body segment (identical movements in cycles shorter than 30 seconds)?
questions.question6: Are tools (approved by EHS) available to carry out the activities, and do they allow the correct grip for the work surface, thus avoiding manual and vibration ergonomic risks?
questions.question7: Does this project / modification have a computer workstation (desktop or laptop) with chairs and tables that meet the ergonomic specifications? Have the ergonomic accessories been provided?
questions.question8: Does the workplace with tasks requiring high-precision inspection have fluorescent or incandescent lighting with good color rendering in addition to general lighting?

questions.numberOfStaff: How many employees perform this activity/workstation on each shift?
questions.scheduleOfWork: What are the working hours? What is the shift regime of the activity? (roster, on-call, etc.)
questions.description: What is the general description of the activity/workstation?
questions.descriptionRelatedActivities: How many tasks does the same employee perform on the shift, besides the assessed task? List them.
questions.timesPerShift: How many times is the activity performed on the shift?
questions.descriptionCompensatoryMechanisms: Are there compensatory mechanisms (breaks, job rotation, workplace exercise, others)? How much time is spent on each?
questions.repeatability: Repetitiveness: of the steps that repeat, in which is the cycle shorter than 30 seconds?
questions.riskFactor: Is there any other risk factor in the activity/workstation (inadequate posture, excessive force, contact stress, cold, vibration)? What is the main body segment involved?
questions.dimensions: Anthropometric dimensions of the workstation (weights, heights, reaches, etc.)
questions.videoMonitor: Is there work with exposure to video monitors? If so, how often and for how long? Is it at the right height?
questions.monotonous: Is the activity monotonous? (little attention required, few stimulus variations, prolonged supervision in a calm environment, fatigue on the night shift)
questions.stress: Are there stressful situations? (excessive workload, pressure, operational changes, etc.)
questions.productivityControl: How is productivity controlled (per month, daily target, etc.)? Is this control strict?
questions.dificulties: Difficulties and complaints reported by the employee.
questions.improvementsAlreadyMade: Improvements already made to the activity/workstation.
questions.measuresForErgonomicToolApplication: Data and measurements for applying the ergonomic tool.
